title: God with us (Matthew 1:18–25)
hook: sleep on it, people say. Joseph had already decided, and then he slept
tomorrow: why would a king be afraid of a baby?

segments.voice: That was a week across a doorway: the chief end, a calling, faith as trust and as showing up, the many rooms, and a family tree that keeps its hard names. Yesterday's line: every name counts.
screen: `EVERY NAME COUNTS.` → `A WEEK ACROSS A DOORWAY.`

segments.voice: Sleep on it. People say it before a big text, a job offer, a breakup. Joseph had already decided. He's promised to Mary, and she is expecting a child that isn't his. Matthew calls him "a just man," and his justice is gentle: he "was minded to put her away privily," to end it quietly, with no public shame. Then, "while he thought on these things," he falls asleep, and the angel of the Lord comes to him in a dream. In this whole chapter, Joseph never says a word.
screen: `SLEEP ON IT.` → `A JUST MAN, MIND MADE UP.` → `AN ANGEL IN A DREAM.`

segments.voice: The angel starts with yesterday's family tree: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." Then Matthew reaches back to words of the prophet Isaiah: "they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." Matthew translates the Hebrew name on the spot. Not God above us. With. In Christian belief, that's what happened in Jesus: God came near, and here he comes near in a worried house, at night. Then Joseph's whole answer, without a speech: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife." The name he gives the boy, Matthew says, is Jesus; Emmanuel is the prophet's word for him. One to tell a friend tonight: Matthew closes the same frame on his last page, with Jesus saying, "lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world." God with us on the first page. I am with you on the last.
screen: `FEAR NOT, THOU SON OF DAVID.` · `EMMANUEL: GOD WITH US.` · `JOSEPH WAKES, AND DOES IT.` · `I AM WITH YOU ALWAY.` · then, large: `GOD WITH US.`

segments.voice: Let one quiet nudge surface: a call you keep meaning to make, an apology, a kindness you shelved. Name it, then name the one thing that keeps stopping you. Then choose the first plain step, small enough to take today, the way Joseph rose and simply did it, and hold that step in mind as you breathe.
Emmanuel. A Hebrew name Matthew translates for us: God with us, on his first page, and kept to his last.
Pocket this one: god with us, and a man who got up and lived it without a word. Week done.
